title: start script depends on dev-only tsx runtime
reasoning: The package declares a compiled entrypoint at dist/cli.js, but npm start executes the TypeScript source through tsx. Since tsx is only in devDependencies, installs that omit dev dependencies, which is common for production or release environments, will not have the tsx binary available and npm start will fail before the CLI starts.
reproduction: Run `npm install --omit=dev` or `pnpm install --prod`, then run `npm start`; the script requires the dev-only `tsx` executable.
recommendation: Make the release start path use a runtime artifact such as `node dist/cli.js` and add/verify a build step that produces it, or move `tsx` into dependencies if this package intentionally starts from TypeScript source in production.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were linked for this package script, and the configured test command exercises TypeScript tests rather than a production install with devDependencies omitted.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a release smoke check that installs production dependencies only and runs the start command, or at minimum validates that `scripts.start` does not reference binaries declared only in devDependencies.
minimumFixScope: Update package.json scripts and, if needed, package build metadata so `npm start` works in production/release installs.
